summary: This class represents an Employee with three properties: firstname, lastname, and pseudo. Each property has a default value, can be read via a getter method, and can be changed via a setter method that returns the object itself to allow chaining multiple calls together.

explanations.3: This puts the class into the App namespace, which is like organizing it into a folder so there's no naming conflict if another file has a class also called Employee.
explanations.7: The constructor parameters use PHP 8's promoted properties feature — declaring them as 'private' here automatically creates and assigns the class properties, so you don't need to write '$this->firstname = $firstname' separately.
explanations.8: The equals sign provides a default value; if someone creates an Employee without arguments, firstname will be 'John'.
explanations.22: Returning '$this' (the Employee object itself) allows you to chain setter calls like $emp->setFirstName('Jane')->setLastName('Smith').
